text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Albanian Prime Minister Fatos Nano asked his cabinet members to replace deputy ministers and department directors in their ministries, a step he said would guarantee the success of the government platform.

- Defence Minister Sabit Broka told a news conference he would set up a professional army and recruit people on three-year paid contracts. However, the national service of 12 months would be retained.
- The Democratic Party is likely to end its boycott of the parliament and take the 27 seats it won in the June 29 elections.

- Greek Foreign Minister Teodoros Pangallos visiting Tirana is to ask Albania to agree to dual citizenship for the ethnic Greek minority in Albania. He is also expected to propose the setting up of a Greek consulate in the port town of Vlore.
- The European Union and the World Bank will grant Albania $7.0 million to ensure the application of a law on transparency regarding pyramid investment schemes, the paper says.
- The Interior Ministry set up a special police department in Vlore to crack down on several criminal bands terrorising the 80,000 townspeople.
- Italy will send some 600 soldiers to help Albanian police restore order and peace, interior minister Neritan Ceka said.
- Police began a drive to disarm people in the southern towns of Fier and Berat after they stepped up checks of cars and snack bars.

- An editorial attacks President Rexhep Meidani, saying his foreign policy to favour relations with neighbouring Greece is against the interest of Albanians and the Albanian minority living in the Kosovo and Macedonia.
- The Democratic Party urged the political forces to organise a roundtable discussion to fulfil the obligations of the international community.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano told parliament on Monday that his Socialist-led coalition government was fully committed to bring the country back to normality.
- France wants to help Albania to set up a new and modern legal system, the French ambassador to Tirana told Justice Minister Thimio Kondi.

- The European Democratic Union (EDU) will always back the Albanian Democratic Party and its leader Sali Berisha, the EDU leader, former Austrian foreign minister Alois Mock told Berisha in a telephone conversation.
